speed_note: Normal speed begins at level 13. The grammar does not change; the amount that gets dropped does.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: ठीक है। दाल-सब्ज़ी दोनों में आएँगी।
lines.read_as: ṭhiik hai. daal-sabzii donoṁ meṁ aaeṁgii.
lines.english: Fine. Dal and sabzi come with both.

learn.explanation_en: From this level the dialogues run at normal conversational speed. Nothing about the grammar changes; what changes is how much gets left out. Line 1 has no verb of ordering at all — लगा दो literally means "put it on" and does the entire job. Line 3 is three words and a request. A dhaba exchange is short because both people already know the script, and that is exactly what makes it hard to follow the first few times.
listening_notes: दाल-सब्ज़ी दोनों में आएँगी: both nouns are feminine, so the verb comes out feminine plural.
थाली is feminine, but दो थाली stays unmarked. A counted noun after a number often does not take a plural ending.
पानी की बोतल — की because बोतल is feminine. The water is masculine and has no say in it.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: दाल-सब्ज़ी दोनों में ___ ।
game.explanation_en: दाल and सब्ज़ी are both feminine, so the verb is feminine plural.

audio.notes_for_recording: Noticeably faster than levels 1 to 12. Clatter and other orders audible.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It'll be ready in ten minutes.

learn.explanation_en: क्या-क्या means "what all", asking for a list rather than a single item. Hindi doubles words to mean various or several — कौन-कौन for "who all", कहाँ-कहाँ for "everywhere in particular". It is not emphasis; it is plurality. You will hear it constantly in exactly this situation, where you want the whole of what is available rather than one dish.
listening_notes: दस मिनट में — में for a period after which something happens. के बाद would mean once ten minutes have elapsed, which is subtly different.
बन जाएगी — कढ़ी is feminine, and the जाना vector makes it definite rather than merely likely.
तो छोले ही दे दो — तो opening a conclusion, ही narrowing it to just that, and दे दो as a compound imperative. Three layers of small words in five syllables.

options: He waits ten minutes for the kadhi
practice.explanation_en: Line 5: तो छोले ही दे दो — the kadhi would take ten minutes.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: दस मिनट ___ बन जाएगी।
game.explanation_en: में for a span of time after which something is done.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 2 rattled off as a list. Line 3 is two words, half-swallowed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: रोटियों के साथ थोड़ा अचार भी।
lines.read_as: roṭiyoṁ ke saath thoṛaa achaar bhii.
lines.english: A bit of pickle with the rotis too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: अचार तो फ़्री है, ले लीजिए।
lines.read_as: achaar to frii hai, le liijie.

learn.title_en: दो रोटी, but रोटियों के साथ
learn.explanation_en: Line 1 has दो रोटी — unmarked, because a counted noun after a number usually stays that way. Line 3 has रोटियों — the full oblique plural, because के साथ is a postposition and postpositions force the oblique regardless of anything else. The same noun, two lines apart, in two different shapes, and the difference is entirely about what follows it. This is the clearest demonstration in the module of why the oblique is a grammatical requirement rather than a meaning.
listening_notes: गरम ला रहा हूँ drops the object entirely — both of them know what is being brought.
अचार तो फ़्री है — तो marking contrast: as for the pickle, it's free.
ले लीजिए — the लेना vector on a polite imperative: take it, it's yours.

practice.question_en: What does the customer learn about the pickle?
options: It comes only with the thali

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: ___ के साथ थोड़ा अचार भी।
game.explanation_en: के साथ is a postposition, so the plural goes oblique.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 4 is generous and slightly amused.

summary.recap_en: Normal speed means more gets dropped, not that the grammar changes. क्या-क्या asks for a list rather than an item. And दो रोटी against रोटियों के साथ shows the oblique doing its job: it is what follows the noun that decides the shape, not what it means.
summary.next_up_en: Next: a proper restaurant, and the first dialogue with three people talking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: नमस्ते सर, कितने लोगों के लिए?
lines.read_as: namaste sar, kitne logoṁ ke lie?

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: तीन के लिए। खिड़की के पास मिल जाएगी?
lines.read_as: tiin ke lie. khiṛkii ke paas mil jaaegii?
lines.english: Three. Could we get one by the window?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: हाँ जी, इधर आइए। मेन्यू ले आता हूँ।
lines.read_as: haaṁ jii, idhar aaie. menyuu le aataa huuṁ.
lines.english: Yes, this way. I'll bring the menu.

learn.title_en: भिजवा दीजिए — a causative doing politeness
learn.explanation_en: भिजवाना is the second causative of भेजना, to have something sent. पानी भी भिजवा दीजिए is "have water sent as well", which is softer than पानी दीजिए because it does not ask the person in front of you to fetch it personally. Causatives do a lot of quiet politeness work in service situations: you ask for the outcome to be caused rather than instructing the individual. It is the same move you will see again in level 15 with बनवा दीजिए.
listening_notes: कितने लोगों के लिए? — लोग goes oblique to लोगों before के लिए, and कितना follows it to कितने.
मिल जाएगी is feminine because टेबल is understood and never said, exactly as कमीज़ was in level 5.
ले आता हूँ is a compound of लाना with आना — "I'll go and bring it". Present tense doing immediate future again.

practice.question_en: What does the customer ask for besides a table?

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: कितने ___ के लिए?
game.explanation_en: के लिए is a postposition, so लोग goes oblique to लोगों.

audio.notes_for_recording: Indoor, quiet, professional. The waiter's lines are smooth and quick.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: सर, हमारा बटर चिकन फ़ेमस है।
lines.read_as: sar, hamaaraa baṭar chikan femas hai.
lines.english: Our butter chicken is famous, sir.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: पनीर टिक्के। लोगों को बहुत पसंद आते हैं।
lines.read_as: paniir ṭikke. logoṁ ko bahut pasand aate haiṁ.
lines.english: Paneer tikka. People like them a lot.

learn.title_en: पसंद आना — a second way of liking
learn.explanation_en: Module 10 gave you मुझे यह पसंद है, a settled preference. पसंद आना is different: it means something appealed, went down well, struck you favourably. लोगों को बहुत पसंद आते हैं — people take to them. The experiencer is still in the dative and the thing is still the subject, so the agreement works exactly as it did, but पसंद आना is about the moment of liking rather than the standing fact. In a restaurant that distinction matters: पसंद है is what you always order, पसंद आया is what you thought of tonight's.
listening_notes: पनीर टिक्के लोगों को बहुत पसंद आते हैं: टिक्के is masculine plural, so आते हैं. लोगों को is को-marked and controls nothing.
वेज में? is two words doing the work of "and what about the vegetarian options?"
ले आइए — the same लाना-plus-आना compound as the previous dialogue, now in the polite imperative.

practice.question_en: What does the waiter recommend for a vegetarian?
practice.explanation_en: Line 4: पनीर टिक्के, in answer to वेज में?

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: लोगों को बहुत पसंद ___ हैं।
game.explanation_en: टिक्के is masculine plural and it is the subject, so आते हैं.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 3 is clipped almost to nothing. Line 6 overlaps the end of line 5.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: मैंने तो पहले ही देख लिया — दाल मखनी।
lines.read_as: maiṁne to pahle hii dekh liyaa — daal makhnii.

lines.speaker: C
lines.hindi: मेरे लिए कुछ भी। तुम ऑर्डर कर दो।
lines.read_as: mere lie kuchh bhii. tum ôrḍar kar do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: ठीक है। भैया, एक दाल मखनी, एक पनीर, चार रोटी।
lines.read_as: ṭhiik hai. bhaiyaa, ek daal makhnii, ek paniir, chaar roṭii.
lines.english: Right. One dal makhani, one paneer, four rotis.

learn.title_en: Three voices, and who is being spoken to
learn.explanation_en: This is the module's first three-speaker dialogue, and the difficulty is not the grammar — it is tracking who is addressing whom. A uses तुम लोग to both friends in line 1. C hands the decision back to A with तुम in line 3. And in line 4 A switches to भैया, which tells you without any other signal that the waiter has arrived and is now being addressed. Three different addressees in six lines, marked entirely by the pronoun and the vocative. Listening for those two things is how you follow a group conversation.
listening_notes: मैंने तो पहले ही देख लिया: ने because देखना is transitive and perfective, तो for emphasis, ही for "already, precisely".
मँगवा लो — the second causative of मँगाना, "have it sent for". Compound imperatives are how friends instruct each other.
तुम लोग is how you address a group informally. लोग here is doing nothing but pluralising तुम.

practice.question_en: Who decides what C will eat?
options: A orders for him, because C does not mind
practice.explanation_en: Line 3: मेरे लिए कुछ भी। तुम ऑर्डर कर दो — C hands it to A.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: ___ तो पहले ही देख लिया — दाल मखनी।
game.question_read_as: ___ to pahle hii dekh liyaa — daal makhnii.
game.explanation_en: देखना is transitive and the tense is perfective, so ने.

audio.notes_for_recording: THREE distinct voices, clearly separated in pitch. Lines 2 and 3 should slightly overlap. Line 4 is directed away from the table.

summary.recap_en: Causatives do politeness work in restaurants — भिजवा दीजिए and मँगवा लो ask for an outcome rather than instructing a person. पसंद आना is liking as a reaction, against Module 10's पसंद है for a standing preference. And with three speakers, the pronoun and the vocative are the only things telling you who is being addressed.
summary.next_up_en: Next: spice levels, ingredients you cannot eat, and checking whether something is really vegetarian.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Have it made with less chilli.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: नहीं, मेरे लिए। तीखा नहीं खा पाता।
lines.read_as: nahiiṁ, mere lie. tiikhaa nahiiṁ khaa paataa.
lines.english: No, for me. I can't manage spicy food.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Fine, we'll have it made mild.

learn.title_en: बनवा देंगे — asking for it to be made differently
learn.explanation_en: बनवाना is the second causative of बनाना, to have something made. कम मिर्च बनवा दीजिए asks for the dish to be made with less chilli by whoever is cooking, rather than instructing the waiter to go and cook. Same politeness move as भिजवा दीजिए in the last level: the causative lets you ask for an outcome without ordering the person in front of you. Note खा पाता in line 3 — पाना from Module 11, "can't manage", which is gentler than नहीं खा सकता because it blames your capacity rather than refusing.
listening_notes: हल्की बनवा देंगे: देंगे agrees with an unstated हम — restaurants habitually speak about themselves in the plural.
तीखा नहीं खा पाता drops both the subject and the auxiliary. At normal speed that is completely usual.
हल्की is feminine because the dish, सब्ज़ी, is understood and never named.

practice.question_en: Who is the mild dish for?

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: ठीक है, हल्की बनवा ___ ।
game.explanation_en: The unstated subject is हम — the restaurant speaking about itself in the plural.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 3 is faintly embarrassed. Line 4 is brisk and reassuring.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Does this have onion in it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes sir, both onion and garlic.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: मैं नहीं खाता। बिना प्याज़ का कुछ है?
lines.read_as: maiṁ nahiiṁ khaataa. binaa pyaaz kaa kuchh hai?
lines.english: I don't eat those. Anything without onion?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It doesn't go in the dal and rice.

learn.title_en: इसमें, and the क्या that sits at the end
learn.explanation_en: इसमें is इस plus में, "in this". Hindi fuses में onto the demonstratives just as it fuses को: इसमें, उसमें, इनमें, उनमें. And the क्या at the end of line 1 turns a statement into a yes-no question — इसमें प्याज़ है क्या? is the same as इसमें प्याज़ है? but a shade more casual. That trailing क्या is everywhere in speech and it is easy to miss, because it arrives after you have already decided the sentence was a statement.
listening_notes: बिना प्याज़ का — बिना means "without" and takes का or के after the noun it governs.
नहीं पड़ता — पड़ना here means "to be put in", a third sense alongside the obligation and involuntary ones you already know.
मैं नहीं खाता, with the auxiliary dropped, states a rule about yourself rather than a decision about tonight.

practice.question_en: What does the customer end up ordering?
options: Something with garlic but no onion
practice.explanation_en: Line 4 says onion does not go in the dal-chawal, and line 5 orders it.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: दाल-चावल ___ नहीं पड़ता।
game.explanation_en: में for an ingredient being inside a dish.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 1's क्या comes late and light. Line 3 is matter-of-fact, not apologetic.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: ये पूरी तरह वेज है ना?
lines.read_as: ye puurii tarah vej hai naa?

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: इन चीज़ों में अंडा तो नहीं?
lines.read_as: in chiizoṁ meṁ anḍaa to nahiiṁ?
lines.english: There's no egg in these, is there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: नहीं सर, हमारी किचन अलग है।
lines.read_as: nahiiṁ sar, hamaarii kichan alag hai.
lines.english: No sir, our kitchen is separate.

learn.title_en: ना at the end — checking, not asking
learn.explanation_en: ये वेज है ना? is not really a question; it is a request for confirmation — "this is veg, right?". ना at the end expects agreement and softens what would otherwise sound like an interrogation. Compare the क्या at the end of the previous dialogue, which asks a genuine yes-no question with no expectation either way. Two single syllables in the same position doing opposite jobs, and both of them arrive after you have already parsed the sentence.
listening_notes: इन चीज़ों में: चीज़ goes to the oblique plural चीज़ों and यह goes to इन. Both change before में.
अंडा तो नहीं? — तो marking contrast, and the question is elliptical: "there isn't egg, is there".
तसल्ली हो गई — तसल्ली is feminine, so गई. The phrase means "now I'm satisfied".

options: The waiter checks with the kitchen
The dish is labelled on the menu

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: इन ___ में अंडा तो नहीं?
game.explanation_en: में is a postposition, so the plural चीज़ें goes oblique to चीज़ों.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 1's ना is short and rising. Line 3 is quieter, almost confidential.

summary.recap_en: Causatives ask for an outcome without instructing a person — बनवा दीजिए. पाना softens an inability into a limit. And two single syllables at the end of a sentence do opposite jobs: क्या asks a real question, ना asks you to agree.
summary.next_up_en: Next: when the order is wrong, and paying the bill.
